name: What is the difference between partial and full pool demolition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between partial pool demolition and full pool demolition, and which one is better for a future remodel or sale?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between partial pool demolition and full pool demolition, and which one is better for a future remodel or sale?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partial and full pool demolition solve different problems. Partial demolition, often called pool fill-in, removes the top portion of the pool shell, drills drainage holes, and backfills the space. It is usually faster and less expensive. Full demolition removes the entire pool structure, including the shell, which creates more usable soil conditions and fewer unknowns for future construction. Full removal is often preferred when a homeowner plans major landscaping, an addition, or a new structure in the same area. Partial removal can be enough for basic yard recovery, but it may leave buried concrete in place. The right choice depends on future site plans, local permit rules, soil conditions, and budget. If a property may be remodeled later, full removal usually offers more long-term flexibility even though the upfront cost is higher.
